messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Synthetic check failure: canary/synthetic-textgen-us-west-2 returning 5xx and latency spike > 3s across 60s window. PagerDuty: PD-98765 - page fired
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-98765 created and routed to #incidents. Escalation policy: primary SRE -> secondary -> infra.
alex.sre: ack. I’m looking. Which canary job?
maya.platform: alex, canary id synth-ct-14, runs against model-proxy pool model:redwood-7b-quant. Fail started ~ 1773001180 (about 1m before alert).
alex.sre: seeing repeated 502s in model-proxy logs, stack traces show upstream grpc: 'resource exhausted' and OOM-kill on worker-12. tail logs: ```Mar 14 01:00:10 model-proxy[pid]: upstream: grpc error: resource exhausted
Mar 14 01:00:11 worker-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4821 (python) total-vm: 12G```.
samira.ops: tagging infra-ops. Possible bad rollout of quantized weights? We pushed q4mm yesterday.
zev: pinging deploy-bot history -> deploy-bot: rollout model:redwood-7b-quant v2 -> started 1772999000 -> completed 1773001100 to canary pool.
maya.platform: canary traffic is small but health-checks run every 30s; if canary instances crash, synthetic check flips quickly.
alex.sre: mitigation plan: 1) remove canary traffic to pool model:redwood-7b-quant 2) spin a replacement with previous non-quant variant 3) collect logs and mark as P1 if customer impact beyond canary. I'll do step 1 now.
alex.sre: `curl -X POST https://internal-routing/api/v1/route/remove -d '{"pool":"canary-us-west-2","model":"redwood-7b-quant"}'` -> response 200
maya.platform: confirming: canary removed from traffic. Starting fallback: routing to model:redwood-7b-v1 (non-quant).
samira.ops: infra-ops, can you check worker-12 host i-0a12b34cd? It hit OOM and rebooted. Recreate instance?
infra-ops: investigating host i-0a12b34cd. It went into kernel OOM and systemd restarted the container. We see elevated GPU memory allocation around the time of rollout. Snapshotting /var/log/messages and dmesg.
zev: are we seeing customer facing errors? Any production routes affected?
maya.platform: initial check: this canary is synthetic-only, no direct customer traffic routed. However we do use canary to detect platform regressions — if it’s failing we should treat as potential regression. No active customer errors in telemetry (error budget still fine).
alex.sre: marking incident as SEV3 for now (canary failure, no customer impact). Will escalate to SEV2 if production routes show errors or if fallback doesn't stabilize.
samira.ops: next steps executed: revert quantized model from canary, scaled up canary pool to 4 healthy hosts to let checks re-run. Also opened a PD incident note: "reverted q4mm canary after OOMs".
alex.sre: collecting detailed logs and heap profiles. Attaching grep snippets: ```grep -i oom /var/log/messages | tail -n 20```.
zev: thanks. Please keep an eye on any correlated autoscaling events or sudden traffic spikes.
maya.platform: after routing change, synth checks regained green within 90s. synthetic check timestamps: fail at 1773001180 -> recovered at 1773001320.
alex.sre: good. I'll run a quick canary replay against the reverted model and watch memory graphs.
infra-ops: host i-0a12b34cd shows kernel OOM policy killed python worker. Disk & GPU health are OK. Suspect q4mm memory footprint higher on certain sequences. We’ll add guardrails in the scaler to limit per-worker token-window memory.
samira.ops: tagging eng-runtime to validate quantization memory regression in CI. samira.ops -> @eng-runtime-team: please take a look at q4mm v2 telemetry.
alex.sre: creating follow-up ticket: INC-2026-037 - quantization v2 caused OOM on canary. Assigning to eng-ml + eng-runtime.
zev: do we need to notify customers? Not necessary since no user impact. Notify sales if anything changes.
alex.sre: handoff to oncall-night in 30m. Current status: canary green, model reverted, hosts stable. Postmortem requested if we confirm the rollout caused regression.
oncall-night: ack received. I’ll monitor overnight for any reoccurrence and verify the remediation stays in place. If canary flips again, escalate to SEV2 and page infra oncall.
alex.sre: quick timeline for the thread: alert 1773001234 -> removal of canary pool 1773001285 -> recovery observed 1773001320 -> root cause investigation ongoing.
maya.platform: adding logs and metrics to the PD incident. Setting follow-up meeting for root-cause analysis.
samira.ops: closing the active paging chain in PD for now, marking as mitigated. Will await postmortem. :white_check_mark:
alex.sre: thanks everyone — summary for postmortem: canary failure caused by increased memory usage in q4mm v2 quantized model; reverted canary -> recovery; no customer impact observed. Assigned INC-2026-037 to eng-ml + eng-runtime.
incident-bot: PD-98765 status: mitigated. Incident will be auto-closed in 72h unless updated.
